summary: A Tonto National Forest lookout on Pinal Peak; the register lists it as a gone ground site, but a 1947 survey describes a steel tower there.

facts.design: steel lookout tower about 80 feet high, per a 1947 survey description
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as gone and ground level. A 1947 survey describes a steel lookout tower there. No source gives a removal date.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station as the center of a Forest Service steel lookout tower about 80 feet high, about nine miles airline south of Globe
Survey station recovered in good condition; the recovery note concerns the survey mark, not the tower

evidence.supports: ground-level lookout Pinal Peak (Ferndell), Gila County, listed as gone
the site is on Tonto National Forest land

evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1947 (DHK)

evidence.supports: steel lookout tower about 9 miles airline south of Globe
evidence.quote: STEEL LOOKOUT TOWER LOCATED ABOUT 9 MILES AIRLINE SOUTH OF GLOBE

evidence.supports: 2022 recovery: survey station recovered in good condition

evidence.supports: radio masts and towers on both peaks today
evidence.quote: Today there are radio masts and towers on both Pinal and Signal Peaks.

evidence.supports: Signal Peak lookout built 1934, replacing a 1920 wooden tower
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, it replaced a wooden tower dating to 1920.

corrections.why: The 1947 survey description calls the structure a steel lookout tower about 80 feet high, while the Forest Fire Lookout Association list calls the site ground level. Whether a tower still stood after 1947 is not known. Confidence is medium.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says ground level. The 1947 survey description says a steel lookout tower about 80 feet high. The story reports both and does not settle which is right for the site today.

sources.title: Pinal Peak Lookout Tower, NGS datasheet DU1996

notes_for_editor: Two conflicts. First, the FFLA list says ground level, but the NGS 1947 description says steel tower; the proposed correction is medium confidence. Second, the record says gone, but the 1947 description and the 2022 recovery note do not say whether the tower still stands; the 2022 note is about the survey mark only. No build year, staffing, fires or removal date found. A HikeArizona forum topic (search snippet only; the page returned 403 and was not read) says the Big Lake marker coordinates belong to the Ferndell/Pinal Peak tower. Not used or verified. Worth trying: Globe newspapers, Tonto National Forest history files, and the original 1947 NGS description for photographs.
